skill.name: gdpr-data-handling
skill.description: Guides GDPR-aware consent, data subject request, retention, privacy design, and breach response implementations with examples and compliance checklists.

security_audit.summary: All 22 static findings are false positives caused by method names, generic database calls, dictionary keys, checklist text, and Markdown formatting. The documentation contains no executable shell or network behavior and no prompt injection. However, the DSAR sample omits server-side verification and authorization checks before personal data access or deletion.

remediation.issue: The DSAR examples do not enforce identity verification or request authorization before data disclosure or deletion.
remediation.suggestion: Require server-side identity proofing, bind requests to authenticated subjects, authorize every operation, and gate processing on verified status.

semantic_findings.title: DSAR Authorization Controls Are Missing
semantic_findings.description: The examples accept verification state from a caller, then process access and erasure requests by identifier without enforcing verified status or authenticated ownership.

content.value_statement: GDPR implementation requires coordinated consent, data rights, retention, and breach controls. This skill provides practical patterns and checklists for planning and reviewing those controls.
actual_capabilities: Explains GDPR personal data categories, lawful bases, and data subject rights.
Provides consent recording and preference interface examples.
Outlines access, erasure, portability, and retention workflows.
Shows privacy by design and data minimization patterns.
Supplies breach response logic and a GDPR implementation checklist.
limitations: Provides general technical guidance, not legal advice.
Examples require authentication, authorization, encryption, testing, and integration before production use.
Does not assess jurisdiction-specific laws or organization-specific processing activities.
Does not connect to databases, identity systems, regulators, or notification services.

use_cases.title: Implement Consent Controls
use_cases.description: Design consent records, preference controls, withdrawal history, and downstream change events for a web application.

use_cases.title: Plan Data Subject Requests
use_cases.description: Map access, erasure, portability, verification, deadlines, and data source coordination into an operational workflow.

use_cases.title: Review Breach Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess notification triggers, reporting content, timelines, and compliance checklist gaps before an incident occurs.

prompt_templates.title: Explain GDPR Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which GDPR principles apply to [processing activity]. Identify personal data, likely lawful bases, and important questions for legal review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a GDPR review for one processing activity.

prompt_templates.title: Design Consent Management
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a consent flow for [product]. Include separate purposes, clear choices, withdrawal, policy versioning, audit history, and accessibility considerations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when planning a new consent interface and storage model.

prompt_templates.title: Create a DSAR Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authenticated DSAR workflow for [system]. Cover intake, identity verification, authorization, discovery, exceptions, deadlines, approval, delivery, and audit evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when coordinating data subject requests across multiple systems.

prompt_templates.title: Review a GDPR Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [architecture description] for GDPR risks. Evaluate minimization, purpose limitation, retention, security, processor relationships, transfers, rights handling, and breach readiness.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced architecture and control review.

output_examples.input: Review our analytics consent process for GDPR readiness.
output: Finding: Analytics remains disabled until the user makes a clear choice.
Gap: Withdrawal does not propagate to downstream analytics tools.
Action: Add consent versioning, propagation monitoring, and an auditable withdrawal record.

output_examples.input: Plan a customer data access request workflow.
output: Intake: Record the request and calculate the response deadline.
Verification: Confirm identity before searching or disclosing personal data.
Delivery: Use an authenticated channel and retain evidence of approval and completion.
Trigger: Evaluate risk to individual rights and freedoms.
Timeline: Escalate immediately and track the 72-hour supervisory authority deadline.
Evidence: Document facts, impact, decisions, notifications, and remediation.

best_practices: Verify identity and authorization before accessing, exporting, correcting, or deleting personal data.
Document each processing purpose, lawful basis, retention rule, recipient, and control owner.
Treat sample code as a design reference and complete security, testing, and legal review before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not use preselected consent or combine unrelated purposes into one choice.
Do not expose DSAR data through identifiers alone or trust caller-provided verification flags.
Do not retain personal data indefinitely or claim anonymization without validating reidentification risk.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides technical guidance and should be reviewed by qualified privacy or legal professionals.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Use them as design references. Add authentication, authorization, encryption, error handling, testing, monitoring, and environment-specific integrations.

faq.question: Does the skill process data subject requests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It outlines workflows and examples but does not connect to identity, database, approval, or delivery systems.

faq.question: Which technologies do the examples use?
faq.answer: The playbook includes JavaScript, HTML, and Python examples with abstract database and service interfaces.

faq.question: Does it cover international data transfers?
faq.answer: It mentions transfer safeguards in the checklist but does not perform transfer impact assessments or select legal mechanisms.

faq.question: How should deadlines and legal bases be validated?
faq.answer: Confirm them against current law, regulator guidance, processing context, and advice from qualified privacy professionals.
